B06_00: Convergent FGF signalling through FGFR1, with WNT, NODAL and BMP input, induces the transcription factors EOMES and TBXT, which switch on SNAI1. SNAI1 represses the genes holding an epithelium together, including E-cadherin, occludin and claudins, so junctions dissolve, cells detach from the basement membrane and ingress, and a mesenchymal expression programme with N-cadherin takes over. A partial version of the same switch leaves adhesion only partly remodelled.
B06_01: Inherited chromatin states are erased so a new transcriptional programme can begin. One genome loses DNA methylation actively, through TET3-mediated oxidation of 5-methylcytosine with deamination and base excision repair; in the other, DPPA3 blocks TET3 recruitment and displaces UHRF1 so DNMT1-dependent maintenance fails and methylation is diluted passively across divisions. KDM5 and KDM6 demethylases trim H3K4me3 and H3K27me3, progressively opening chromatin.
B06_02: Hedgehog ligands SHH and IHH arriving from neighbouring cells switch on the forkhead transcription factor FOXF1, which marks the responding cells once specified. FOXF1 then drives BMP4 expression, and BMP4 together with FOXF1 activates GATA4; BMP4 sustains FOXF1 while GATA4 reinforces both its own transcription and that of BMP4. The result is a self-maintaining feedback loop that locks in the new identity before downstream differentiation genes are engaged.
B06_03: NODAL signalling through SMAD2 and SMAD3 cooperates with the pioneer factor FOXH1, with TEAD factors and their coactivator YAP1 released from Hippo restraint, and with the T-box factor TBXT to switch on FOXA2. FOXA2 in turn drives targets such as NOTO and the secreted signal SHH, while WNT input through beta-catenin with LEF1 and TCF7 positions the programme spatially, coupling extracellular signals to a stable transcriptional identity.
B06_04: The M isoform of the transcription factor MITF sets how much oxidative metabolism a cell runs. By inducing PPARGC1A, the coactivator that coordinates mitochondrial biogenesis and respiratory gene expression, it shifts metabolism toward oxidative phosphorylation rather than glycolysis. MITF also raises SIRT1, an NAD+-dependent deacetylase that couples metabolic state to transcription and, by deacetylating substrates including p300, supports proliferation and opposes senescence.
B06_05: The transcription factor MITF-M drives a survival programme by inducing anti-apoptotic targets including BCL2, BCL2A1 and the IAP family member BIRC7. It also induces DICER1, linking it to microRNA biogenesis, and one of its targets hosts the intronic microRNA miR-211, which acts with Argonaute proteins and TNRC6 scaffolds in silencing complexes to shape downstream gene expression. Repressive input through POU3F2 and the SIN3A-HDAC1 corepressor tunes the output.
B06_06: The transcription factor MITF-M acts as a direct repressor of genes governing extracellular matrix organisation, focal adhesion and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition. Lowering its activity releases targets such as the integrin subunit ITGA2, the adhesion scaffold paxillin, the matrix components EDIL3 and peroxidasin, and SERPINE1, alongside the regulators ZEB1, SOX2, CDH1 and CDH2. The result is cytoskeletal remodelling, altered matrix attachment and a mesenchymal-like, migratory character.
B06_07: A progenitor chooses between two alternative epithelial fates according to the interplay of Notch, WNT and hormone receptor signalling, with loss of Notch input biasing it toward the secretory option. Prolactin acting through its receptor and downstream STAT signalling then drives secretory differentiation and expression of secreted protein genes, while neighbouring cells adjust Notch ligand availability. A self-renewing precursor pool persists and can rebuild the secretory compartment later.
B06_08: Strong epidermal growth factor receptor stimulation specifies a contractile epithelial fate, producing cells that contract on hormone stimulation and help deposit the basement membrane they sit on. The ligands amphiregulin, EGF and TGF-alpha set that signal intensity during branching morphogenesis. Such progenitors are normally unipotent, but loss of the adjacent inner cells lets EGFR with Notch and Wnt signalling license them to regenerate that compartment.
B06_09: Regional identity in a sheet of differentiating cells is set first by holding BMP signalling off with secreted inhibitors, after which OTX2, ZIC2 and POU-domain factors including POU3F1 and POU5F1 act on an upstream enhancer to switch on SOX2. SOX1, PAX6, ZEB2 and ZNF521 accompany the exit from pluripotency as NANOG and POU5F1 expression resolves. A sharp boundary is fixed by reciprocal transcriptional repression between OTX2 and GBX2.
B06_10: Previously stockpiled transcripts are cleared on schedule by factors already stored alongside them, handing control of gene expression to newly made products. Two adaptors act in succession, ZFP36L2 then BTG4, each recruiting the multisubunit CCR4-NOT deadenylase, whose CNOT7/CNOT8 and CNOT6/CNOT6L nucleases shorten poly(A) tails and commit messages to decay. BTG4 also links the complex to poly(A)-binding protein and cap-binding machinery, while DICER1-derived siRNAs guide AGO2 to slice complementary transcripts.
B06_11: Transcription from a previously silent genome is switched on after extensive epigenetic remodelling, including DNA demethylation and changes in histone methylation and acetylation, and proceeds as a minor then a major wave. DUX4, promoted by DPPA2 and DPPA4, binds promoters of early genes such as ZSCAN4, LEUTX, DUXA and KDM4E and recruits CREBBP and EP300. It also drives bidirectional transcription from retroviral long terminal repeats and satellite repeats.
B06_12: The transcription factor MITF-M drives targets that keep proliferating cells genomically stable, including the MCM2 and MCM5 subunits of the replicative helicase, the DNA ligase LIG1 that seals nicks during replication and repair, the recombination and damage-response factor BRCA1, and the telomerase catalytic subunit TERT. Depleting MITF lets DNA damage accumulate and drives senescence, whereas ATF4-driven translational suppression of MITF causes reversible arrest instead.
B06_13: Unipotent epithelial progenitors expand and then choose between tubular and secretory destinies according to Notch and steroid hormone receptor signalling, retaining enough plasticity to revert toward a stem-like state when conditions change. The epidermal growth factor receptor ligands amphiregulin, EGF and TGF-alpha act as the paracrine link converting systemic steroid signalling into local proliferation, driving tube elongation and branching alongside fibroblast growth factor cues.
B06_14: In a branching epithelium, committed but undifferentiated precursors are held proliferating until a subset is released toward a hormone-producing fate. ONECUT1 sustains ONECUT3 and HNF1B, which maintain the progenitor state and tube formation, while NEUROG3 induction marks commitment. Notch signalling through NOTCH1, RBPJ and Mastermind-like coactivators, with the acetyltransferases CREBBP, EP300, KAT2A and KAT2B, drives the repressor HES1 to restrain NEUROG3 in neighbours, rationing differentiation.
B06_15: MITF-M expression and activity commit a multipotent precursor to a single fate. Before commitment FOXD3, SOX2 and SNAI2 silence its promoter, with ZIC1, PAX3, SOX9 upstream and HDAC1 aiding relief of repression; afterwards PAX3 and SOX10 bind it, reinforced by WNT/beta-catenin with LEF1, endothelin, KIT and cAMP-CREB input, and MITF-M feeds back to extinguish FOXD3 and SOX2. Phosphorylation, SUMOylation, ubiquitination, 14-3-3 binding, nuclear export and acetylation tune its output.
B06_16: High NODAL signalling acting through SMAD2 and SMAD3 with SMAD4 induces EOMES, MIXL1 and goosecoid, and EOMES in turn switches on FOXA2, SOX17 and the GATA4/GATA6 pair that define the new identity and license later specialised programmes. Unlike cells taking a full epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, these retain E-cadherin rather than switching to N-cadherin, remodelling adhesion so they intercalate into an epithelial sheet; WNT input via beta-catenin and TCF7L2 patterns the step.
B06_17: Periodic segmentation of a mesenchymal sheet arises from a clock-and-wavefront arrangement, in which a molecular oscillator meets gradients of WNT, FGF and retinoic acid that set a determination front. The oscillator is built from Notch negative feedback: HES7 represses its own transcription, and LFNG, induced through NOTCH1 and RBPJ, dampens Notch, with DLL1 and DLL3 shaping the response. At the front, TBX6 and MSGN1 drive MESP2.
B06_18: A hierarchical transcriptional network specifies and maintains an early committed precursor state. HNF1B, ONECUT1 and PDX1 act first and, together with FGF10 signalling from adjacent mesenchymal cells, drive a second tier of factors including PTF1A, ONECUT3, NR5A2 and NKX6-1. These downstream regulators begin to separate the alternative enzyme-secreting and hormone-producing fates, so the network links earlier patterning to later differentiated identity.
B06_19: NODAL signalling through SMAD2, SMAD3 and SMAD4 with the chromatin reader TRIM33 acts with BMP4 and WNT-driven beta-catenin, TCF7 and LEF1 to position a signalling centre and switch on the first lineage transcription factors, TBXT and EOMES. These, with FOXH1, MIXL1 and GSC, specify new lineages while shutting down the pluripotency network of POU5F1, SOX2 and NANOG. One lineage emerges by full epithelial-mesenchymal transition, another partially.
B06_20: A border identity between two alternative fates is positioned by intermediate levels of BMP and FGF with a graded WNT input, so BMP4, FGF4 and WNT3A acting through beta-catenin and TCF7L1 place cells between the two states rather than in either. Within that domain, transcription factors including GBX2, TFAP2A, PAX3, PAX7, MSX1, DLX5 and ZIC1 cross-regulate into a self-reinforcing identity while pluripotency factors resolve.
B06_21: A broadly specified progenitor population is patterned along two axes and directed into a multipotent, more restricted progenitor state, passing through intermediate bipotent states before alternative fates are excluded. Signals from the surrounding mesenchyme and adjacent midline tissue make that choice, and fibroblast growth factors including FGF10 sustain progenitor proliferation and expansion, alongside FGF2, FGF4, FGF7 and EGF acting through receptor tyrosine kinases.
B06_22: Stockpiled transcripts are destroyed by factors that the newly activated genome itself switches on. Partially deadenylated messages, held in a closed-loop translation complex with cap-binding and poly(A)-binding proteins, are tagged at their 3' ends with untemplated uridines by the terminal uridylyltransferases TUT4 and TUT7. The uridine tail recruits PABPN1, which brings in the 3'-to-5' exoribonuclease DIS3L2, linking deadenylation, uridylation and exonucleolytic decay into one programme.
B06_23: Bipotent tube-forming progenitors pass into a committed hormone-producing mid-progenitor state, and the choice is made largely by mechanical cues from the surrounding matrix. Fibronectin and vitronectin engage integrin alpha5beta1, promote spreading and sustain a YAP1-NOTCH mechanosignalling axis that represses commitment, while fibrillar collagens and laminins favour confinement, relieving that repression so NEUROG3 rises and progenitor markers such as SOX9 and ONECUT1 fall. EGF signalling likewise restrains NEUROG3.
B06_24: A stratified epithelium is continuously rebuilt as cells move outward through successive layers. Basal stem cells self-renew and generate transit amplifying cells, which divide several times before committing to progressively more differentiated states, finally discarding nuclei and organelles to become flattened, cross-linked cells that are shed and replaced. Each transition depends on cues from the surrounding microenvironment, with epidermal growth factor signalling favouring basal proliferation and delaying commitment.
B06_25: Growth factor and insulin signalling switches off a stress- and starvation-driven transcriptional programme through AKT-mediated inactivation of FOXO1. Without signalling, FOXO1 shuttles between nucleus and cytoplasm with enough nuclear residence to drive genes for gluconeogenesis, autophagy, cell cycle arrest and apoptosis. Once PI3K activates the AKT isoforms, they phosphorylate FOXO1 at several sites, promoting 14-3-3 binding and nuclear exclusion, so the programme is silenced and growth and survival permitted.
B06_26: The M isoform of the transcription factor MITF sets how mobile a cell is. Through targets such as the adhesion molecule CEACAM1, the actin-nucleating formin DIAPH1 and the purine-metabolic enzyme GMPR, it tunes cell-cell adhesion and the state of the actin cytoskeleton, and it also feeds into epithelial-mesenchymal transition programmes via SNAI2. Cells therefore switch between a high-MITF differentiated, proliferative state and a low-MITF migratory one.
B06_27: The transcription factor MITF-M behaves as a rheostat whose target output shifts with its own activity level. At intermediate activity it drives proliferation, inducing CDK2, cyclin D1, cyclin B1, CDC25B, PLK1 and the kinase MET; falling activity slows the cycle and dedifferentiates cells, while excessive activity induces the CDK inhibitors p21 and p16 and arrests them. Wnt-responsive TCF/LEF factors, TBX2 and SIN3A-HDAC1 set the repressive side.
B06_28: A surface epithelial sheet gives rise to basally located stem cells able to regenerate an entire branched tubular structure and to produce both inner and outer epithelial progeny. These rare, self-renewing bipotent progenitors drive placode and bud formation, tube outgrowth and later remodelling. FGF10 signalling through its epithelial receptor is one of the better-conserved inputs generating and maintaining them, alongside Wnt/beta-catenin, Hedgehog, Notch and hormone signalling.
B06_29: A highly compacted genome packaged with protamines rather than histones must be rebuilt into ordinary chromatin so it can decondense and become transcriptionally permissive. The kinase SRPK1 phosphorylates PRM1 and PRM2, promoting their removal by the nucleoplasmin NPM2 and recruiting the histone chaperone HIRA, which deposits the replacement-independent variant H3.3 with core H2B and H4, H2AX and a specialised linker histone. Arginine methylation of H3.3 by METTL23 supports its incorporation.
B06_30: Besides its differentiation targets, the transcription factor MITF-M drives genes that build and acidify degradative compartments: essentially the whole vacuolar H+-ATPase, both the membrane-embedded V0 sector and the cytosolic V1 ATP-hydrolysing sector, plus an accessory subunit. Proton pumping acidifies lysosomes and endosomes, a precondition for hydrolase activity, cargo degradation, receptor recycling and autophagic flux. MITF also induces the lysosomal acid ceramidase ASAH1, linking sphingolipid turnover to proliferation.
B06_31: Progenitors give rise to short-lived circulating phagocytes that leave their site of production in a CCR2-dependent manner and either die or enter other compartments and differentiate further. Two cytokines set the fate and tone of this output: macrophage colony-stimulating factor drives survival, proliferation and mononuclear phagocyte differentiation through CSF1R, while interferon gamma licenses classical activation, raising antigen presentation and antimicrobial capacity.
B06_32: An epithelial tip meeting a mesenchymal population induces its differentiation: WNT9B makes the progenitors aggregate and express WNT4, driving a mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition into polarised vesicles while a self-renewing progenitor pool persists. WT1 acts at one pole to repress PAX2 and permit one fate, LHX1 and POU3F3 specify the other, and HNF1B activates the Notch components DLL1, JAG1 and LFNG plus IRX1 and IRX2, with HNF4A supporting proximal identity.
B06_33: A transient progenitor population switches on neurogenin 3 and is thereby committed away from alternative fates toward hormone-producing identities. NEUROG3 acts as a short-lived pioneer factor that directly induces a second tier of regulators, including PAX4, NEUROD1, NKX2-2 and INSM1, which consolidate the new identity, drive exit from the cell cycle, and bias progenitors toward particular hormone subtypes. A brief pulse is thus converted into a stable state.
B06_34: The M isoform of MITF switches on the enzymes and structural proteins that build and move pigment granules. It binds M-box elements in promoters of the synthetic enzymes tyrosinase, TYRP1 and DCT and of granule components such as MLANA, PMEL and GPR143, and drives RAB27A, MYO5A and melanophilin, which tether and transport granules toward the periphery. Transcription needs SOX10, TFAP2A, LEF1 with beta-catenin, CREB1 and IRF4, plus BAF/SWI-SNF remodelling.
B06_35: A strip of cells is carved out along the medial-lateral axis by graded BMP signalling, high on one side and low on the other, while WNT, FGF and retinoic acid gradients set its position along the orthogonal axis. OSR1 and LHX1 mark the territory first, then PAX2 and PAX8 act in a mutually reinforcing loop with them. FOXC1 and FOXC2 in neighbouring cells repress LHX1 and OSR1, confining the domain.
B06_36: Posterior identity in a differentiating sheet is built differently from anterior: its caudal portion derives from bipotent progenitors in which WNT and FGF signalling, via WNT3A and FGF8, drive SOX2 through a dedicated posterior enhancer while TBX6 pulls sister cells toward the alternative mesodermal fate. Identity is then fixed by mutual repression between posterior GBX2 and anterior OTX2, with SOX1, ZEB2 and POU3F1 accompanying commitment.
B06_37: Cells of a mesenchymal cord epithelialise in response to signals from adjacent tissue, forming a tube from whose caudal end a new bud emerges and branches. Retinoic acid acting via HOXB4 sets where this happens, while PAX2 and PAX8 with LHX1 mark early progenitors; LHX1 and GATA3 sustain each other in a loop inducing EMX2, ID4, nephronectin and RET. RET responds to GDNF, and nephronectin engages integrin alpha8beta1.
B06_38: A single-layered epithelium lining a branching tube arises from bipotent trunk progenitors, themselves derived from earlier multipotent progenitors, with apical cilia and microvilli marking maturity. The matrix side of the programme is prominent: fibrillar collagens with fibronectin and vitronectin build interstitial stroma, while laminin trimers with collagen IV partners form the basement membrane that polarises the epithelium and positions progenitors for their fate choice.
B06_39: A single epithelial outgrowth sprouts from a duct into adjacent mesenchyme, branches, and induces differentiation at its tips, with reciprocal signalling controlling where it forms. Nephronectin from the duct engages integrin alpha8beta1 to switch on GDNF, which acts through the RET receptor tyrosine kinase with its co-receptor GFRA1 and induces WNT11. PAX2, EYA1, SIX1/SIX2 and SALL1 make the mesenchyme competent, while SLIT2-ROBO2, BMP4 with gremlin and FOXC1/FOXC2 restrict budding.
